definition.title: Radial Velocity Lab
learning_objectives: Connect stellar reflex motion to the mass, period, eccentricity, and inclination of an orbiting companion.
Read a Keplerian radial-velocity curve and identify how eccentricity, phase, and the star's argument of periastron change its shape.
Distinguish the exact spectroscopic mass function and edge-on minimum companion mass from the conventional projected quantity Mp sin i.
Explain why radial velocity alone cannot determine orbital inclination and therefore cannot generally determine the companion's true mass.

fields.name: planet_mass_kg
fields.meaning: True companion mass used by this educational forward model.

fields.name: eccentricity
fields.meaning: Bound-orbit eccentricity inside the reviewed v1 domain.

fields.name: inclination_deg
fields.meaning: Orbital inclination where 0 degrees is face-on and 90 degrees is edge-on.

fields.name: stellar_argument_of_periastron_deg
fields.meaning: Argument of periastron of the star's reflex orbit, using the Doppler convention.

fields.name: mean_anomaly_at_epoch_deg
fields.meaning: Mean anomaly at t=0; the explicit reproducible orbital phase control.

input_schema.invalid_handling: Reject booleans, non-finite values, out-of-range values, companion-to-star mass ratios above 0.1, and angles outside the half-open [0,360) domain. No scientific input is silently clamped or normalized.

output_schema: exact Keplerian stellar radial-velocity semi-amplitude K
conventional projected companion mass Mp sin(i)
exact edge-on minimum companion mass implied by the mass function and stellar mass
301-point deterministic one-period stellar reflex radial-velocity curve

equations.true_anomaly: tan(nu/2) = sqrt((1+e)/(1-e)) * tan(E/2), implemented with a quadrant-safe atan2 equivalent
equations.stellar_reflex_velocity: v_r = K * (cos(nu + omega_star) + e*cos(omega_star)); systemic gamma is defined as zero in this reflex-only lab
equations.edge_on_minimum_mass: Mmin is the unique nonnegative solution of Mmin^3/(Mstar+Mmin)^2 = f for sin(i)=1

definition.sampling_policy: Return exactly 301 samples from t=0 through t=P inclusive. Mean anomaly advances linearly; Kepler's equation is solved deterministically in Python for each sample. The browser must not solve orbital phase or regenerate radial velocities.
definition.default_preset: Illustrative synthetic star/companion system with a one-Julian-year circular edge-on orbit. It is not a named observed system and carries no observational provenance claim.
assumptions: One star and one companion follow an isolated Newtonian two-body Keplerian orbit with constant masses.
The returned velocity is the star's line-of-sight reflex component relative to the system barycenter; systemic velocity gamma is zero by definition.
The star's argument of periastron is used, matching the reviewed Doppler-orbit convention.
Inclination is supplied by the educational forward model even though radial-velocity observations alone do not generally determine it.
The initial mean anomaly is an exact phase input; observational timing uncertainty is not represented.
The synthetic default is educational and is not presented as a fit to a real exoplanet system.
limitations: No additional planets, mutual perturbations, precession, tidal evolution, relativistic corrections, or stellar binary effects.
No stellar activity, granulation, oscillations, tellurics, spectrograph drift, zero-point offsets, cadence effects, measurement uncertainty, or random noise.
V1 restricts eccentricity to <= 0.95 as a conservative product/numerical domain; this is not a physical boundary for all bound exoplanets.
For a circular orbit, periastron and its argument are physically undefined; the argument and mean-anomaly inputs act only as a reproducible phase convention.
The conventional label Mp sin(i) is not algebraically identical to the exact edge-on minimum mass when the companion mass is non-negligible in the mass-function denominator.
A face-on orbit has zero radial-velocity semi-amplitude in this ideal model, so RV alone provides no positive companion-mass lower bound from that signal.

validation_fixtures.purpose: For e=0, omega_star=0, and M0=0 the RV curve is K*cos(2*pi*t/P), giving +K, 0, -K, 0, +K at quarter-period phases.
With all other inputs fixed, K at 30 degrees is one half of K at 90 degrees.
At i=0 the ideal line-of-sight reflex semi-amplitude, mass function, projected mass, and entire RV curve are zero.
At M0=0 and omega_star=0, periastron gives K*(1+e) and half a period later gives K*(-1+e).
The returned exact minimum mass reproduces the returned mass function when inserted into the sin(i)=1 mass-function equation.
The upper reviewed eccentricity boundary produces a finite deterministic curve without phase-solver failure.
Identical canonical inputs return exactly identical immutable results.
Non-finite, bool, angle, mass-ratio, period, eccentricity, and range violations fail closed.
Source, model-version, constant, preset, and validation-contract drift is rejected by the strict loader.

scientific_validation.method: Cross-check limiting circular/eccentric phase cases against the reviewed Keplerian equations, inclination scaling against the explicit sin(i) projection, and the exact minimum-mass solution against the spectroscopic mass function.
